title: Model Catalog Stability Playbook: Soft-Pin Heuristics and Compatibility Signals
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Provide a formal playbook that clarifies acceptance criteria, runtime compatibility signals, and soft-pin heuristics for onboarding new open-model variants into the Redwood model catalog. The playbook defines decision rules for when to pin a variant, when to allow soft-pinned (deprioritized) serving, and the observable signals and rollback triggers that gate promotion to full pinned status.
background: Over the last two quarters we've onboarded multiple community weights with varying stability. Engineering and Ops have requested clearer runbooks for: (1) soft-pin behavior (serve but deprioritize), (2) compatibility metadata required at intake, and (3) deterministic rollback and canary rules to prevent production quality regressions. Current intake docs are fragmented across PRDs and GitHub issues; product needs a single, authoritative contract and acceptance checklist for PM/Eng/DS reviewers.
scope: Define soft-pin semantics and allowed serving behaviors (traffic share, fallback rules)
Specify required compatibility metadata fields and their validation (runtime tags, expected kv-cache format, tokenization info)
Create acceptance criteria and a checklist for onboarding reviewers
Define monitoring SLOs, alerts, and automatic rollback triggers for canary and post-rollout phases
Provide a minimal test harness and synthetic workloads to validate performance & correctness
out_of_scope: Model training and provenance verification beyond declared metadata
Large-scale retraining of existing catalog models
Changes to pricing or commercial contracts for dedicated customers
requirements: Compatibility metadata: architecture, tokenizer, kv-cache-compatibility-version, max-context, supported-quantization-flavors
Compatibility scorecard: automated runtime probe yields a score 0-100 based on latency variance, memory stability, and kv-cache hit behavior
Soft-pin policy: default initial soft-pin = 5% traffic for new variants unless sponsor requests lower bound
Fallback policy: if soft-pin variant fails health checks, traffic instantly routes to pinned fallback variant with no error surface to customers
Pin decision window: require 7-day canary with no critical alerts and scorecard >= 85 to promote to pinned
Rollback triggers: latency p99 > baseline + 150ms sustained for 10 minutes OR quality drift (eval suite) > 3% regression
Documentation: intake PR must include a 'compatibility-notes.md' with explicit answers to a 12-question checklist
Security: models that request syscalls or custom kernels must pass security_review_required flow before pinning
acceptance_criteria: Intake PR present with compatibility-notes.md and sample inference payloads
Automated runtime probe produces scorecard and stores as catalog metadata
Onboarding runbook approved by Eng, Runtime, and Security (signoffs captured in PR)
Canary runner automatically limits traffic per soft-pin policy and emits required metrics to Console
Promote script can only be executed after 7 days of green canary and manual review approval
Rollback policy validated via injected-failure DR test in staging environment
api_fields_and_changes: catalog.ingest: new optional fields -> compatibility_tags (list), kv_cache_version (string), tokenizer_hash (string)
catalog.metrics: store 'compat_score' numeric field and 'canary_start_ts' timestamp
promote endpoint: requires signer token and a review_approval_id to avoid accidental pinning
rollout_plan: Week 0: Merge PRD, implement catalog API fields and compatibility probe (eng-sprint week 0)
Week 1: Add canary runner and Console dashboard widgets for compat_score and rollback alerts
Week 2: Run dry-run with two internal experimental variants; iterate on probe thresholds
Week 3-4: Public beta: onboard 3 community models under soft-pin and collect telemetry
Week 5: Evaluate metrics, publish playbook, and open schedule for wider adoption
qa_tests_and_validation: Synthetic load test validating percentile latency against baseline with 95th percentile pass
KV-cache stability test that simulates long-conversation scenarios and verifies no memory leaks
Behavioral eval suite of 500 prompt pairs measuring top-level regression; automated alerts if regression > 2%
Failure-injection test: simulate kernel fallback and assert fallback route latency < baseline + 100ms
Security checklist run: static analysis of model artifacts and verification of no network egress during inference
open_questions: Should soft-pin default traffic share be configurable per customer or per-variant? (PM/Legal input needed)
How aggressive should the compat_score weighting be for quality vs perf? Proposed weights: quality 50%, latency stability 30%, resource stability 20%
Do we need a separate 'experimental' status for models that opt out of pinning but want higher visibility?
What SLA language do we expose in the Console for soft-pinned variants?
Is 7 days an appropriate promotion window for low-traffic variants?
decisions_to_date: Adopted 'compat_score' as a single numeric shorthand for intake review (decision 2025-02-10)
Soft-pin default = 5% traffic unless variant owner requests otherwise (decision 2025-02-11)
Promotion to pinned requires manual review + 7-day green canary (decision 2025-02-12)
dependencies: ENG-42111: Console metrics and dashboard widgets
SEC-102: security review automation for ingest artifacts
